approachQuestion.prompt:
Two sensors report occupancy for the same 64m slots. Each report is already packed into an array of m unsigned 64-bit words; corresponding bits represent the same slot. Return the number of slots reported occupied by both sensors.

Constraints: 1 <= m <= 200000; all bits represent valid slots.
Example: m=1, A=[13], B=[11] -> 2, because common set positions are 0 and 3. Edge case: A=[0], B=[18446744073709551615] -> 0.

Choose the best approach under these constraints.
constraints: 64-bit AND, OR, XOR and popcount (number of set bits) cost constant time. A count of up to 64m fits in one counter word. The payload word width 64 is fixed.
Inputs are read-only. Include all temporary storage and any call stack; exclude the supplied input and the returned output. No input copy is implicit.

options.text: For each corresponding word pair, popcount their AND and add it to one counter.
options.feedback: AND keeps exactly the slots occupied in both reports; disjoint word blocks contribute independent counts.

options.text: Expand both reports into Boolean arrays of 64m entries, then count positions where both Booleans are true.
options.feedback: Expansion preserves the answer but stores per-slot arrays instead of directly processing the packed input.

options.text: Sum popcounts of the OR of each corresponding word pair.
options.feedback: OR counts occupancy by either sensor. A=[1], B=[0] gives 1 instead of 0.

options.text: Count occupied slots separately in A and B, then return the smaller count.
options.feedback: The sets can be disjoint even with equal counts: A=[1], B=[2] requires zero, not one.

feedback.reason: AND identifies jointly occupied slots, and popcount counts each once.
details: Scan the two existing packed arrays in parallel. For each word position, intersect the words using AND, count the set bits in that word, and accumulate the result.
AND identifies jointly occupied slots, and popcount counts each once. The reports are already packed, so no unpacked 64m-slot structure is needed. The count must aggregate all m word intersections.
“For each corresponding word pair, popcount their AND and add it to one counter.”: AND keeps exactly the slots occupied in both reports; disjoint word blocks contribute independent counts.

“Expand both reports into Boolean arrays of 64m entries, then count positions where both Booleans are true.”: Expansion preserves the answer but stores per-slot arrays instead of directly processing the packed input.
“Sum popcounts of the OR of each corresponding word pair.”: OR counts occupancy by either sensor. A=[1], B=[0] gives 1 instead of 0.
“Count occupied slots separately in A and B, then return the smaller count.”: The sets can be disjoint even with equal counts: A=[1], B=[2] requires zero, not one.

feedback.reason: Process m packed word pairs with constant AND/popcount work each.
details: Each of m word pairs incurs constant AND and popcount work. Only the loop index, intersection word and counter are auxiliary.
64-bit AND, OR, XOR and popcount (number of set bits) cost constant time. A count of up to 64m fits in one counter word. The payload word width 64 is fixed.
“O(m) time, O(m) auxiliary space”: This includes unnecessary unpacked arrays, absent from the analyzed method.
“O(m²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Only corresponding word pairs are compared.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: An unread word pair can change the total.
